full_judgment:
2. The land in question was transferred by a kabala dated 18-1-78 and registered on Respondents sought pre-emption claiming to be co-sharers or the vendor; the application for pre-emption was resisted on a number of grounds, such as, it was barred by limitations the transfer was not pre-emptable the apparent purchaser was a mere benamder of his father who was a co-sharer of the vendor. These grounds were accepted the trial Court which dismissed the application; but on appeal, its decision was reversed and pre-emption was allowed by the Additional District Judge, Netrakona; against his decision the petitioner came the High Court in revision but became unsuccessful. 

 3. Dr. .Ahmed Husain learned Advocate for the petitioner has urged before us the ground of limitation only. He has questioned the view of the High Court Division that for the purpose of preemption the date of transfer will be the date of registration of the kabala, whereas under Section 47 of the Registration Act, a transfer takes effect from the date of execution of the kabala. This is a question which has been long settled by a series of decisions to the effect that 'transfer' within the meaning of section 96 of the state Acquisition Act, is completed when a certificate is issued by the registering officer that the document has been registered. Registration is a process which is completed on the date this certificate is issued. This has nothing to do with the date from which the transfer takes effect. For the purpose of filing an application for pre-emption, it is the date of registration which is of material importance. The next question urged by the learned Advocate is that in this case the respondents knew of the transfer long before the date of registration, and as such limitation will start from the date of this knowledge. There is hardly any substance in this argument for, the right to pre-emption accrues on the date the kabala is registered, and from this date, the application for pre-emption in this case was filed within the prescribed time.
